blocks.text: Introduction

Assalam o alaikum bachon! Aaj hum Unit 8 shuru kar rahe hain: Mathematical Induction and Binomial Theorem. Is unit ka pehla hissa ek bilkul naye qisam ka saboot (proof) sikhata hai. Ab tak hum ne zyada tar sawal hal kiye hain: koi value nikaali, koi equation hal ki. Ab hum yeh seekhenge ke koi formula har natural number ke liye sach hai, yeh kaise saabit kiya jaye. Misal ke taur par, aap ne sequences and series mein parha hoga ke \(1 + 2 + 3 + \ldots + n = \frac{n(n + 1)}{2}\). Lekin kya humein yaqeen hai ke yeh \(n = 1000\) ya \(n = 1{,}000{,}000\) par bhi sahi hai? Har number par check karna to namumkin hai. Mathematical induction yahi masla hal karta hai.

Kitab batati hai ke Francesco Maurolico (1494-1575) ne induction ka tareeqa ijaad kiya aur sab se pehle is se yeh saabit kiya ke pehle \(n\) odd (taaq) musbat integers ka sum \(n^{2}\) hota hai. Unhon ne integers ki bohat si properties pesh keen aur un mein se kuch ko mathematical induction se saabit kiya. Theoretical computer science mein bhi yeh tareeqa bohat ahem hai: algorithms (kaam karne ke qadam ba qadam tareeqe) design karne, un ki durusti (correctness) jaanchne aur un ki complexity (kitna waqt lagta hai) ka andaza lagane mein yahi soch kaam aati hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab naam "Mourolico" likhti hai; aam taur par yeh Maurolico likha jata hai. Induction tab istemal hota hai jab koi baat har natural number \(n\) ke liye claim ki jaye: koi sum ka formula, koi divisibility (taqseem hone) wali baat, ya koi inequality. Hum la-mehdood (infinite) numbers ek ek kar ke check nahin kar sakte, is liye aisa saboot chahiye jo ek hi dafa mein sab numbers ko cover kar le.

Hum jaante hain ke kisi mathematical formula ke khilaf sirf ek misaal (exception) bhi us formula ko ghalat saabit karne ke liye kaafi hai. Aisi misaal jis par formula ya statement fail ho jaye, counter example (ulti misaal) kehlati hai. Yaad rakhiye: kisi baat ko sach saabit karne ke liye saboot chahiye, lekin ghalat saabit karne ke liye sirf ek counter example kaafi hai.

Jo formula ya statement kisi variable par munhasir ho, aur woh variable kisi set se aata ho, woh tab hi durust maana jata hai jab woh us set ke har element ke liye sach ho. Yani "zyada tar" sach hona kaafi nahin, "har ek" ke liye sach hona zaroori hai.

Misal ke taur par yeh statement dekhiye: \(S(n) = n^{2} - n + 41\) har natural number \(n\) ke liye prime number (aisa number jo sirf 1 aur khud se taqseem ho) hai. Pehle chand natural numbers ke liye \(n^{2} - n + 41\) ki values neeche table mein di gayi hain:

blocks.caption: \(S(n) = n^{2} - n + 41\) ki values, pehle gyarah natural numbers ke liye

blocks.text: Table dekh kar lagta hai ke yeh statement kaafi had tak sach ho sakti hai: 41, 43, 47, 53, ... sab prime hain. Lekin agar hum agle natural numbers par check karte jayein to \(n = 41\) par yeh statement fail ho jati hai; yani \(n = 41\) ek counter example hai. Is se hum yeh nateeja nikaalte hain ke chand khaas misaalon ko dekh kar baghair saboot ke aam formula bana lena aqalmandi nahin. Yeh misaal mashhoor mathematician Euler (1707-1783) ne dhoondi thi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dekhte hain \(n = 41\) par kya hota hai. \(n = 41\) rakhiye:
\[S(41) = 41^{2} - 41 + 41\]
\[= 41^{2} = 41 \times 41 = 1681\]
1681 ko 41 poora poora taqseem karta hai, is liye yeh prime nahin. Hairat ki baat yeh hai ke \(n = 1\) se \(n = 40\) tak har value prime aati hai! Yani chalees (40) sahi misaalein bhi baat ko sach saabit nahin kar sakeen.
Kyun: chand misaalein sirf andaza (guess) deti hain, saboot nahin. Isi liye humein ek pakka saboot chahiye jo har \(n\) ko cover kare, aur mathematical induction aisa hi saboot hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text:
Rozmarra zindagi se ek misaal: aap ne apne mohalle ke das kawwe dekhe, sab kaale the. Kya yeh saabit ho gaya ke duniya ka har kawwa kaala hai? Nahin. Sirf yeh pata chala ke ab tak jo dekhe woh kaale the. Agar kahin ek safaid kawwa mil jaye to woh poora daawa toot jata hai. Maths mein bhi yahi hota hai: das, bees ya chalees misaalein daawe ko pakka nahin kartin, lekin ek counter example use ghalat saabit kar deta hai.
Is liye exam mein agar poocha jaye "saabit kijiye ke har \(n\) ke liye ..." to sirf chand values rakh kar dikhana saboot nahin maana jata. Wahan induction (ya koi aur pakka saboot) chahiye. Haan, agar poocha jaye "dikhaiye ke yeh baat ghalat hai", to ek counter example kaafi hai.
Ab ek aur misaal lete hain aur nateeja banane ki koshish karte hain. Humein pehle \(n\) odd natural numbers ka sum maloom karna hai. Pehle chand sums likh kar pattern (tarteeb ka andaaz) dekhte hain:

blocks.caption: Pehle \(n\) odd (taaq) natural numbers ke sums

blocks.text:
Sums ki sequence yeh hai: \((1)^{2}, (2)^{2}, (3)^{2}, (4)^{2}, \ldots\) Dekhiye, har sum us mein shamil terms ki tadaad ka square hai: 3 terms ka sum \(3^{2} = 9\), 4 terms ka sum \(4^{2} = 16\). Is liye yeh statement sach lagti hai. Har natural number \(n\) ke liye:
\[1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots + (2n - 1) = n^{2} \quad \ldots \text{(i)}\]
kyun ke \(n\)th odd number \(= 1 + 2(n - 1) = 2n - 1\) hai (pehla term 1, har dafa 2 barhta hai).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab statement (i) ko \(1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots - (2n - 1) = n^{2}\) chhapti hai aur saath "\(n\)th term \(= 1 - 2(n - 1)\)" likhti hai. Dono jagah sign ghalat chhapa hai. Sahi:
\[1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots + (2n - 1) = n^{2}\]
\[a_{n} = 1 + 2(n - 1) = 2n - 1\]
Tasdeeq: \(n = 3\) par \(2(3) - 1 = 5\), jo teesra odd number hai. Kitab wala \(1 - 2(3 - 1) = -3\) deta hai, jo ghalat hai.

Lekin statement (i) ko har positive integer \(n\) ke liye check karna mumkin nahin, kyun ke is ke liye la-mehdood hisaab karna parega jo kabhi khatam nahin hoga. Aap 6 tak check kar sakte hain, 100 tak, shayad computer se ek arab tak, lekin "har" \(n\) tak kabhi nahin.

Mathematical induction ka tareeqa isi mushkil se bachne ke liye istemal hota hai. Aam taur par yeh set \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}\) (natural numbers) se mutalliq statements ya formulas saabit karne ke liye hota hai, lekin kabhi kabhi set \(\{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\}\) (whole numbers) wali statements ke liye bhi istemal hota hai. Example 4 mein aap aisi hi ek statement dekhenge jo \(n = 0\) se shuru hoti hai.

Hypothesis: Hypothesis (mafrooza) ek soocha samjha andaza ya mujawwaza wazahat hai jo mehdood saboot (evidence) ki buniyad par kisi baat ke baare mein di jaye. Yeh mazeed tehqeeq ka nuqta-e-aaghaz hota hai aur tajurbaat aur mushahide se test kiya ja sakta hai. Science ki research mein hypothesis aam taur par aisi statement ki shakal mein likha jata hai jise test kiya ja sake, aur data us ki ya to taeed kare ya use radd kar de.

Induction of Hypothesis: Is se muraad woh amal hai jis mein khaas misaalon ya khaas soorton mein nazar aane wale patterns ko dekh kar ek aam statement ya hypothesis banaya jata hai. Yeh technique aksar mathematical reasoning (riyazi daleel) mein conjectures (aise andaze jo abhi saabit nahin hue) pesh karne ke liye istemal hoti hai, jinhein baad mein deductive methods (pakki mantiqi daleel) se poori tarah saabit kiya jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono misaalon ko saath rakh kar dekhiye. Prime wali misaal mein 11 soorton se pattern andaza kiya gaya aur woh ghalat nikla. Odd numbers wali misaal mein 6 soorton se pattern andaza kiya gaya aur woh sahi hai. Pattern dekh kar andaza lagana "induction of hypothesis" hai: yeh humein ek aisi baat deta hai jo saabit karne ke qabil hai, lekin khud saboot nahin.
Ab ek misaal se induction ka asal idea samjhiye. Dominoes (khari tikyon) ki ek lambi qatar sochiye. Agar (1) pehla domino gir jaye, aur (2) har domino girte hue apne agle domino ko gira de, to qatar ke tamam dominoes gir jayenge, chahe qatar kitni hi lambi ho. Mathematical induction bilkul isi tarah kisi baat ko tamam \(n\) ke liye saabit karta hai. Ek aur misaal: seedhi (ladder). Agar aap pehli seerhi par charh sakte hain, aur har seerhi se agli par charh sakte hain, to aap har seerhi tak pohanch sakte hain.

Hypothesis aur induction of hypothesis ka farq ek baar phir saaf kar lete hain, kyun ke naam milte julte hain. Hypothesis ek andaza hai, maslan "pehle \(n\) odd numbers ka sum \(n^{2}\) hai". Induction of hypothesis woh amal hai jis se yeh andaza bana: hum ne 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 terms ke sums dekhe, pattern nazar aaya, aur aam baat bana li. Science mein bhi yahi hota hai: scientist tajurbe dekh kar hypothesis banata hai, phir mazeed tajurbon se use test karta hai. Maths mein farq yeh hai ke hum sirf tajurbon par bharosa nahin karte; hum pakka mantiqi saboot dete hain. Mathematical induction woh saboot hai jo pattern ko "andaze" se "pakki haqeeqat" bana deta hai.
8.1 Principle of Mathematical Induction
Mathematical induction ka usool (principle) yun bayan kiya jata hai: agar koi proposition ya statement \(S(n)\), har positive integer \(n\) ke liye, aisi ho ke

items: Base Case: \(S(1)\) sach ho, yani \(n = 1\) par \(S(n)\) sach ho, aur
Induction of Hypothesis: jab bhi kisi positive integer \(k\) ke liye \(S(k)\) sach ho, to \(S(k + 1)\) bhi sach ho,
Conclusion: to \(S(n)\) tamam positive integers ke liye sach hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sirf do cheezein check karne se la-mehdood soortein kaise saabit ho gayin? Base case se \(S(1)\) sach hai. Ab doosri sharat mein \(k = 1\) rakhiye: \(S(1)\) sach hai, is liye \(S(2)\) sach hai. Phir \(k = 2\): \(S(2)\) sach hai, is liye \(S(3)\) sach hai. Aur yeh silsila chalta rehta hai:
\[S(1) \Rightarrow S(2) \Rightarrow S(3) \Rightarrow \cdots\]
Koi bhi positive integer is zanjeer se bahar nahin reh jata.
Kyun dono qadam zaroori hain: base case ke baghair zanjeer shuru hi nahin hoti (pehla domino gira hi nahin), aur doosre qadam ke baghair zanjeer aage nahin barhti (domino agle ko nahin girata).
Dhyan dein: doosre qadam mein hum \(S(k)\) ko saabit nahin karte. Hum use farz (assume) karte hain, aur is farz ko induction hypothesis kehte hain. Kaam sirf yeh dikhana hai ke agar \(S(k)\) sach ho to \(S(k + 1)\) zaroor sach hoga.
Procedure for Induction of Hypothesis

items: \(n = 1\) rakh kar dikhaiye ke statement \(n = 1\) ke liye sach hai.
Farz kijiye ke statement kisi positive integer \(k\) ke liye sach hai, phir dikhaiye ke yeh agle integer \(k + 1\) ke liye bhi sach hai.

blocks.text:
Doosri sharat ke liye in do tareeqon mein se koi ek istemal kiya ja sakta hai:
\(S(k + 1)\) ko \(S(k)\) ki madad se saabit kiya jaye.
\(S(k)\) par algebraic amal (jaise dono taraf koi term jama karna) kar ke \(S(k + 1)\) tak pohancha jaye.
Neeche ki tamam misaalon mein aap dekhenge ke hum aksar doosra tareeqa istemal karte hain: \(S(k)\) ke dono taraf agla term jama kar ke \(S(k + 1)\) bana lete hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sum wale har induction saboot ko likhne ka ek pakka tareeqa, jo exam mein bhi poore number dilata hai:
1. Statement ko \(S(n)\) ka naam dein.
2. Base case: \(S(1)\) check karein; left side aur right side alag alag hisaab kar ke barabar dikhaein.
3. \(S(k)\) likhein aur use (A) ka naam dein.
4. \(S(k + 1)\) likhein, us ki right side simplify karein aur use (B) kahein. Yeh aap ki manzil (target) hai.
5. (A) ke dono taraf \((k + 1)\)th term jama karein aur right side ko simplify karte jayein jab tak (B) ki right side na ban jaye.
6. Conclusion likhein.
Kyun target pehle likhein: jab manzil maloom ho to raasta asaan ho jata hai; aap ko pata hota hai ke algebra kis shakal par khatam karni hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text:
Agla term kaise nikaalein, yeh induction ka sab se nazuk qadam hai. Har series ka ek general term hota hai jo \(n\) par munhasir hota hai:
Example 1 mein general term \(3n\) hai, to \((k + 1)\)th term \(3(k + 1)\) hai.
Example 2 mein general term \(n^{2}\) hai, to \((k + 1)\)th term \((k + 1)^{2}\) hai.
Example 4 mein general term \(3 \cdot 5^{n}\) hai, to agla term \(3 \cdot 5^{k + 1}\) hai.
Tareeqa hamesha ek hi hai: general term mein \(n\) ki jagah \(k + 1\) rakh dijiye. Kabhi bhi andaze se "agla number" mat likhiye.
Ab kitab ki misaalein dekhte hain. Har misaal mein teen hisse pehchaniye: base case, hypothesis aur step, aur conclusion.

Exam mein induction ka sawal aam taur par 5 se 8 numbers ka hota hai, aur examiner har hisse ke alag number deta hai: base case ke, hypothesis likhne ke, step ki algebra ke, aur conclusion ke. Is liye har hissa saaf heading ke saath likhiye: "Base Case", "Induction of Hypothesis", "Conclusion". Bohat se bachay algebra to theek kar lete hain magar aakhri jumla (conclusion) likhna bhool jate hain, aur number kat jate hain. Ek aur mashwara: \(S(k + 1)\) ki right side pehle simplify kar ke likh lijiye; phir step ke aakhir mein jab wahi shakal aa jaye to saaf likhiye "yeh (B) ki right side hai". Is se examiner ko foran nazar aata hai ke aap ne manzil haasil kar li.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: Use mathematical induction to prove that \(3 + 6 + 9 + \ldots + 3n = \frac{3n(n + 1)}{2}\) for every positive integer \(n\).
steps:
Given: \(S(n): 3 + 6 + 9 + \ldots + 3n = \frac{3n(n + 1)}{2}\).
To prove: \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye sach hai.
Method: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke yeh "har \(n\) ke liye" wali baat hai, is liye mathematical induction lagayenge: pehle \(n = 1\), phir \(S(k)\) farz kar ke \(S(k + 1)\) saabit karenge.

Step 1: Base case (n = 1)
Left side: sum \(3n = 3\) par ruk jata hai, yani sirf pehla term 3.
\[\text{Right side} = \dfrac{3(1)(1 + 1)}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{6}{2} = 3\]
Dono taraf 3 aaya, is liye \(S(1)\) sach hai, yani base case poora ho gaya.
Kyun: base case mein dono sides alag alag hisaab kar ke barabar dikhani hoti hain. Sirf "true hai" likh dena kaafi nahin.

Step 2: Induction hypothesis
Farz karein ke kisi \(n = k \in \mathbb{N}\) ke liye \(S(n)\) sach hai, yani
\[3 + 6 + 9 + \ldots + 3k = \dfrac{3k(k + 1)}{2} \quad (A)\]
Kyun: yeh woh farz hai jise hum istemal kar sakte hain. Ise saabit nahin karna, sirf is se aage barhna hai.

Step 3: n = k + 1 par statement (hamari manzil)
\(3k\) ke baad agla term \(3(k + 1)\) hai:
\[3 + 6 + \ldots + 3k + 3(k + 1)\]
\[= \dfrac{3(k + 1)[(k + 1) + 1]}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(k + 1)(k + 2)}{2} \quad (B)\]
Kyun: \(S(n)\) mein har jagah \(n\) ki jagah \(k + 1\) rakh diya. Agla term \(3(k + 1) = 3k + 3\) hai, \(3k + 1\) nahin; general term \(3n\) mein \(n = k + 1\) rakhne se yahi aata hai.

Step 4: (A) ke dono taraf 3(k + 1) jama karein
\[3 + 6 + \ldots + 3k + 3(k + 1)\]
\[= \dfrac{3k(k + 1)}{2} + 3(k + 1)\]
Kyun: (A) ki left side mein agla term jama karne se bilkul (B) ki left side ban jati hai. Right side par (A) wala farz kaam aata hai. Jo left par jama kiya, wahi right par bhi jama karna zaroori hai, warna barabari toot jayegi.

Step 5: Common factor 3(k + 1) bahar nikaalein
\[= 3(k + 1)\left(\dfrac{k}{2} + 1\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{3(k + 1)(k + 2)}{2}\]
Yani agar \(S(k)\) sach ho to \(S(k + 1)\) bhi sach hai.
Kyun: dono terms mein \(3(k + 1)\) maujood hai. Use bahar nikaalne se \(\frac{k}{2} + 1 = \frac{k + 2}{2}\) bachta hai, aur yeh bilkul (B) ki right side hai. Sab kuch multiply kar ke kholne se behtar hai ke pehle common factor nikaalein.

Step 6: Conclusion
Dono sharatein poori ho gayin, is liye mathematical induction se \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye sach hai.
Kyun: base case ne zanjeer shuru ki aur Step 5 ne har \(k\) se \(k + 1\) tak pohanchaya.

Tasdeeq:
\(n = 3\): left side \(3 + 6 + 9 = 18\); right side \(\frac{3(3)(4)}{2} = 18\). Dono barabar, formula sahi hai.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(3 + 6 + 9 + \ldots + 3n = \frac{3n(n + 1)}{2}\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 1 mein "Adding \(3(k + 1)\) on both the sides of (A)" wali line mein kitab \(3 + 6 + 9 - \ldots + 3k + 3(k + 1)\) chhapti hai. Yeh minus chhapai ki ghalti hai; sahi \(3 + 6 + 9 + \ldots + 3k + 3(k + 1)\) hai, kyun ke sum ke tamam terms jama ho rahe hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Pehle khud koshish kijiye, phir jawab dekhiye.
1. Example 1 mein \(n = 5\) par dono sides kya aati hain? (Jawab: \(3 + 6 + 9 + 12 + 15 = 45\), aur \(\frac{3 \cdot 5 \cdot 6}{2} = 45\).)
2. Agar koi student Step 4 mein sirf left side par \(3(k + 1)\) jama kare aur right side par na kare, to kya hoga? (Jawab: barabari khatam ho jayegi; equation ke dono taraf hamesha ek hi cheez jama ki jati hai.)
3. Ek student ne Step 3 mein agla term \(3k + 1\) likh diya. Us ki ghalti kahan hai? (Jawab: series 3, 6, 9, ... mein har term 3 ka multiple hai; agla term general term \(3n\) mein \(n = k + 1\) rakhne se \(3(k + 1) = 3k + 3\) aata hai. \(3k + 1\) to 3 ka multiple bhi nahin, is liye woh series ka term ho hi nahin sakta.)

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.problem: Use mathematical induction to prove that for any positive integer \(n\), \(1^{2} + 2^{2} + 3^{2} + \ldots + n^{2} = \frac{n(n + 1)(2n + 1)}{6}\).
steps:
Given: \(S(n): 1^{2} + 2^{2} + 3^{2} + \ldots + n^{2} = \frac{n(n + 1)(2n + 1)}{6}\).
To prove: \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye sach hai.
Method: induction; step mein agla square \((k + 1)^{2}\) jama karenge. Yeh squares ke sum ka mashhoor formula hai jo aage bohat kaam aayega.

Step 1: Base case (n = 1)
\[S(1): (1)^{2} = \dfrac{1(1 + 1)(2 \times 1 + 1)}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 \times 2 \times 3}{6} = 1\]
Dono taraf 1, is liye \(S(1)\) sach hai, base case poora.
Kyun: left side \(1^{2} = 1\), right side bhi 1 deti hai.

Step 2: Induction hypothesis
Farz karein ke kisi \(k \in \mathbb{N}\) ke liye \(S(k)\) sach hai:
\[1^{2} + 2^{2} + \ldots + k^{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{k(k + 1)(2k + 1)}{6} \quad (A)\]
Kyun: yahi farz hamara sahara hai.

Step 3: S(k + 1) likhein (hamari manzil)
\[1^{2} + 2^{2} + \ldots + k^{2} + (k + 1)^{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{(k + 1)(k + 1 + 1)(2(k + 1) + 1)}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{(k + 1)(k + 2)(2k + 3)}{6} \quad (B)\]
Kyun: \(n\) ki jagah \(k + 1\) rakha; \(2(k + 1) + 1 = 2k + 3\). Kitab \(k + 1\) ke upar lakeer (bar) laga kar likhti hai; yeh bracket ka purana tareeqa hai, matlab \(2(k + 1) + 1\).

Step 4: (A) ke dono taraf (k + 1)^2 jama karein
\[1^{2} + 2^{2} + \ldots + k^{2} + (k + 1)^{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{k(k + 1)(2k + 1)}{6} + (k + 1)^{2}\]
Kyun: is se (A) ki left side (B) ki left side ban jati hai.

Step 5: (k + 1) ko common nikaalein, denominator 6 rakhein
\[= \dfrac{(k + 1)[k(2k + 1) + 6(k + 1)]}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{(k + 1)(2k^{2} + k + 6k + 6)}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{(k + 1)(2k^{2} + 7k + 6)}{6}\]
Kyun: \((k + 1)^{2}\) ko \(\frac{6(k + 1)^{2}}{6}\) likhein to dono terms mein \(\frac{k + 1}{6}\) common hai. Agar hum sab kuch khol dete to \(k^{3}\) wala lamba polynomial banta aur ghalti ka khatra barhta.

Step 6: Quadratic ke factors banaein
\[2k^{2} + 7k + 6 = 2k^{2} + 4k + 3k + 6\]
\[= (k + 2)(2k + 3)\]
\[\therefore \; = \dfrac{(k + 1)(k + 2)(2k + 3)}{6}\]
Yani formula \(k + 1\) ke liye bhi sach hai.
Kyun: \(7k\) ko \(4k + 3k\) mein todha kyun ke \(4 \times 3 = 12 = 2 \times 6\) (middle term break ka tareeqa). Waise bhi (B) se humein pehle se pata tha ke factors \((k + 2)\) aur \((2k + 3)\) aane chahiyein; manzil ne raasta dikha diya.

Step 7: Conclusion
Dono sharatein poori hain, is liye mathematical induction se di gayi statement tamam positive integers ke liye sach hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(n = 3\): \(1 + 4 + 9 = 14\) aur \(\frac{3 \cdot 4 \cdot 7}{6} = \frac{84}{6} = 14\). Barabar.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(1^{2} + 2^{2} + \ldots + n^{2} = \frac{n(n + 1)(2n + 1)}{6}\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 2 ka formula istemal kar ke \(1^{2} + 2^{2} + \ldots + 10^{2}\) maloom kijiye. (Jawab: \(\frac{10 \cdot 11 \cdot 21}{6} = 385\).)
Ab sochiye: agar induction ke baghair hum yeh formula sirf \(n = 1, 2, 3\) par check karte, to kya yeh kaafi hota? Nahin! \(n^{2} - n + 41\) wali misaal yaad kijiye. Induction ne hi is formula ko har \(n\) ke liye pakka kiya.

Ab tak ki dono misaalein sums ki theen. Agli misaal mein statement mukhtalif hai: humein dikhana hai ke ek fraction hamesha poora number (integer) banta hai. Tareeqa wahi induction hai, lekin step mein soch thori badal jati hai.

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.problem: Show that \(\frac{n^{3} + 2n}{3}\) represents an integer \(\forall n \in \mathbb{N}\).
steps:
Given: \(S(n) = \frac{n^{3} + 2n}{3}\).
To prove: har natural number \(n\) ke liye \(S(n)\) integer hai.
Method: induction. Step mein \(S(k + 1)\) ko do hisson mein todenge: ek \(S(k)\), aur doosra aisa hissa jo saaf saaf integer ho.

Step 1: Base case (n = 1)
\[S(1) = \dfrac{1^{3} + 2(1)}{3} = \dfrac{3}{3}\]
\[= 1 \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Base case poora hua.
Kyun: 1 integer hai (\(\mathbb{Z}\) integers ka set hai).

Step 2: Induction hypothesis
Farz karein ke kisi \(n = k \in \mathbb{N}\) ke liye \(S(k) = \frac{k^{3} + 2k}{3}\) integer hai.
Kyun: yahi farz aage istemal hoga.

Step 3: S(k + 1) ko kholein
Ab dikhana hai ke \(S(k + 1)\) bhi integer hai. \(n = k + 1\) rakhne par:
\[S(k + 1) = \dfrac{(k + 1)^{3} + 2(k + 1)}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{k^{3} + 3k^{2} + 3k + 1 + 2k + 2}{3}\]
Kyun: identity \((a + b)^{3} = a^{3} + 3a^{2}b + 3ab^{2} + b^{3}\) se \((k + 1)^{3} = k^{3} + 3k^{2} + 3k + 1\).

Step 4: Terms ko is tarah jorhein ke S(k) nazar aaye
\[= \dfrac{(k^{3} + 2k) + (3k^{2} + 3k + 3)}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{(k^{3} + 2k) + 3(k^{2} + k + 1)}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{k^{3} + 2k}{3} + (k^{2} + k + 1)\]
Kyun: hum ne jaan boojh kar \(k^{3} + 2k\) ko alag kiya, kyun ke yahi \(S(k)\) ka upar wala hissa hai. Baqi tamam terms mein 3 ka factor hai, jo neeche wale 3 se cancel ho jata hai. Yeh chaal (trick) aise sawalon ki jaan hai.

Step 5: Dono hisse integers hain
\(\frac{k^{3} + 2k}{3}\) hamare farz ke mutabiq integer hai, aur \(k^{2} + k + 1\) bhi integer hai kyun ke \(k\) natural number hai. Do integers ka sum integer hota hai, is liye \(S(k + 1)\) integer hai. Yani statement \(k + 1\) ke liye bhi sach hai.
Kyun: integers ko jama karne se kabhi fraction nahin banta.

Step 6: Conclusion
Dono sharatein poori hain, is liye mathematical induction se \(\frac{n^{3} + 2n}{3}\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye integer hai.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\frac{n^{3} + 2n}{3}\) har \(n \in \mathbb{N}\) ke liye integer hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Do numbers ke darmiyan dot (.) zarb (multiplication) ka nishan hai. (Yeh box Example 4 ke saath chhapa hai: \(3.5^{2}\) ka matlab \(3 \times 5^{2}\) hai, "teen point paanch" nahin. Hum ise \(3 \cdot 5^{2}\) likhte hain.)

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Use mathematical induction to prove that \(3 + 3.5 + 3.5^{2} + \ldots + 3.5^{n} = \frac{3(5^{n + 1} - 1)}{4}\), whenever \(n\) is a non-negative integer.
steps:
Given: \(S(n): 3 + 3 \cdot 5 + 3 \cdot 5^{2} + \ldots + 3 \cdot 5^{n} = \frac{3(5^{n + 1} - 1)}{4}\) (dot ka matlab zarb hai).
To prove: \(S(n)\) har non-negative integer \(n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots\) ke liye sach hai.
Method: induction, lekin is dafa base case \(n = 0\) se, kyun ke statement \(n \ge 0\) ke liye claim ki gayi hai.

Step 1: Base case (n = 0)
\(n = 0\) par left side mein sirf pehla term \(3 \cdot 5^{0} = 3 \cdot 1 = 3\) hai. Right side:
\[\dfrac{3(5^{0+1} - 1)}{4} = \dfrac{3(5 - 1)}{4} = 3\]
Dono taraf 3, is liye \(S(0)\) sach hai, base case poora.
Kyun: yahan pehli value 0 hai, 1 nahin. Zanjeer wahin se shuru hoti hai jahan se statement shuru ho. Yaad rakhiye \(5^{0} = 1\).

Step 2: Induction hypothesis
Farz karein ke kisi non-negative integer \(k\) ke liye \(S(k)\) sach hai:
\[3 + 3 \cdot 5 + \ldots + 3 \cdot 5^{k}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(5^{k + 1} - 1)}{4} \quad (A)\]
Kyun: yahi farz aage kaam aayega. (Kitab \(k \in N\) likhti hai, lekin yahan \(k\) koi bhi whole number ho sakta hai, 0 samait.)

Step 3: S(k + 1) likhein (hamari manzil)
\(3 \cdot 5^{k}\) ke baad agla term \(3 \cdot 5^{k + 1}\) hai:
\[3 + 3 \cdot 5 + \ldots + 3 \cdot 5^{k} + 3 \cdot 5^{k + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(5^{(k + 1) + 1} - 1)}{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(5^{k + 2} - 1)}{4} \quad (B)\]
Kyun: har jagah \(n\) ki jagah \(k + 1\) rakha. Power mein \(n + 1\) tha, to ab \(k + 2\) ho gaya.

Step 4: (A) ke dono taraf 3·5^(k+1) jama karein
\[3 + 3 \cdot 5 + \ldots + 3 \cdot 5^{k} + 3 \cdot 5^{k + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(5^{k + 1} - 1)}{4} + 3 \cdot 5^{k + 1}\]
Kyun: left side ab (B) ki left side ban gayi.

Step 5: Right side ko simplify karein
\[= \dfrac{3(5^{k + 1} - 1 + 4 \cdot 5^{k + 1})}{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{3[5^{k + 1}(1 + 4) - 1]}{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(5^{k + 2} - 1)}{4}\]
Yeh dikhata hai ke jab \(S(k)\) sach ho to \(S(k + 1)\) bhi sach hai.
Kyun: \(3 \cdot 5^{k + 1} = \frac{3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5^{k + 1}}{4}\) likhne se 3 aur 4 dono common ban jate hain. Phir \(5^{k + 1}\) ke do hisse jama hue: \(1 \cdot 5^{k + 1} + 4 \cdot 5^{k + 1} = 5 \cdot 5^{k + 1} = 5^{k + 2}\) (powers ka qaida: same base par powers jama hoti hain).

Step 6: Conclusion
Dono sharatein poori hain, is liye mathematical induction ke usool se \(S(n)\) har \(n \in W\) (whole numbers 0, 1, 2, ...) ke liye sach hai.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(3 + 3 \cdot 5 + \ldots + 3 \cdot 5^{n} = \frac{3(5^{n + 1} - 1)}{4}\) har non-negative integer \(n\) ke liye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 4, base case: kitab power \(5^{0-1}\) chhapti hai; sahi \(5^{0+1}\) hai (tab hi \(\frac{3(5 - 1)}{4} = 3\) banta hai, jaisa kitab agle qadam mein khud likhti hai).
Example 4, \(S(k + 1)\): left side ka aakhri term \(3.5^{k-1}\) chhapa hai; sahi \(3.5^{k+1}\) hai.
Hypothesis mein kitab \(k \in N\) likhti hai, lekin statement \(n = 0\) se shuru hai, is liye \(k\) koi bhi whole number (\(k \in W\)) hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text:
Example 4 se ek ahem sabaq: base case hamesha us pehli value se shuru hota hai jis se statement shuru ho rahi hai. Sawal mein "non-negative integer" likha tha, yani 0, 1, 2, 3, ..., is liye hum ne \(n = 0\) check kiya. Agar hum sirf \(n = 1\) check karte to \(n = 0\) wali soorat saabit hi na hoti, aur saboot adhoora reh jata.
Aage 8.1.1 mein aap dekhenge ke kuch statements \(n = 2\) ya \(n = -2\) jaisi values se shuru hoti hain. Wahan bhi yahi qaida hai: jahan se daawa shuru, wahin se base case.
Ek aur baat: \(3.5\) ko point wala number (teen point paanch) samajhna bohat aam ghalti hai. Is kitab mein do numbers ke beech dot ka matlab zarb hai. Shak ho to pehla term check kar lijiye: \(n = 0\) par sum 3 hona chahiye, aur \(3 \cdot 5^{0} = 3\) hi aata hai.

Ab ek naye qisam ka sawal: divisibility. "9 se divisible" ka matlab hai ke number 9 ka koi poora multiple hai, jaise 9, 18, 27, 81. Is qisam ke sawal mein sab se ahem chaal yeh hai ke farz ko ek equation ki shakal mein likha jaye.

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem: Prove that \(4^{n} + 6n - 1\) is divisible by 9 for all \(n \in \mathbb{N}\).
steps:
Given: \(S(n) = 4^{n} + 6n - 1\).
To prove: har natural number \(n\) ke liye \(S(n)\) 9 se poora taqseem hota hai.
Method: induction. "9 se divisible" ko "9 guna koi integer" likhenge, phir is equation ko \(S(k + 1)\) mein substitute karenge.

Step 1: Base case (n = 1)
\[S(1) = 4^{1} + 6(1) - 1\]
\[= 4 + 6 - 1 = 9\]
9 to 9 se divisible hai, is liye \(n = 1\) par baat sach hai.

Step 2: Induction hypothesis
Farz karein \(n = k\) par statement sach hai, yani \(S(k) = 4^{k} + 6k - 1\) 9 se divisible hai. (A)
Is ka matlab hai ke kisi integer \(k_{1}\) ke liye \(4^{k} + 6k - 1 = 9k_{1}\), yani
\[4^{k} = 9k_{1} - 6k + 1\]
Kyun: divisibility ko equation bana kar hum \(4^{k}\) ki jagah kuch aur rakh sakte hain. Sirf lafzon mein "divisible hai" likhne se algebra aage nahin barhti.

Step 3: n = k + 1 rakhein
\[S(k + 1) = 4^{k + 1} + 6(k + 1) - 1\]
\[= 4 \cdot 4^{k} + 6k + 6 - 1\]
Kyun: \(4^{k + 1} = 4 \cdot 4^{k}\). Is tarah woh cheez \(4^{k}\) samne aa gayi jis ke baare mein humein maloom hai.

Step 4: Hypothesis se 4^k ki value rakhein
\[= 4(9k_{1} - 6k + 1) + 6k + 6 - 1\]
\[= 36k_{1} - 24k + 4 + 6k + 5\]
\[= 36k_{1} - 18k + 9\]
\[= 9(4k_{1} - 2k + 1) \quad (B)\]
Yeh 9 se divisible hai.
Kyun: \(36k_{1}\), \(18k\) aur 9 teeno 9 ke multiples hain, is liye 9 bahar nikal aaya. Bracket ke andar \(4k_{1} - 2k + 1\) ek integer hai, kyun ke \(k_{1}\) aur \(k\) integers hain.

Step 5: Conclusion
Yani jab \(S(k)\) sach ho to \(S(k + 1)\) bhi sach hai. Dono sharatein poori hain, is liye mathematical induction se statement tamam integers \(n \ge 1\) ke liye sach hai.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(4^{n} + 6n - 1\) har \(n \in \mathbb{N}\) ke liye 9 se divisible hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text:
Example 3 aur Example 5 dono "poora number" ya "divisible" wale sawal hain, magar chaal mukhtalif hai:
Example 3 mein \(S(k + 1)\) ko kholne ke baad hum ne \(S(k)\) wala hissa alag kar diya aur dekha ke baqi hissa saaf integer hai.
Example 5 mein \(4^{k}\) ko kisi aur hisse se alag karna mushkil tha, is liye hum ne farz ko equation (\(4^{k} = 9k_{1} - 6k + 1\)) bana kar seedha substitute kar diya.
Exam mein jo tareeqa aasan lage woh istemal kijiye; dono durust hain. Ahem baat yeh hai ke aakhir mein 9 (ya 3) ko bahar nikaal kar dikhaein, aur bataein ke bracket ke andar wali cheez integer hai.

Ab kitab ki aakhri misaal is hisse ki. Is mein sigma (\(\sum\)) ka nishan aata hai jo shayad naya lage, lekin ghabraiye nahin: \(\sum\) sirf "jama karo" ka chhota nishan hai. \(\sum_{k=1}^{n}\) ka matlab hai ke \(k = 1\) se shuru kar ke \(k = n\) tak har value rakh kar term banao aur sab jama karo. Is misaal mein fractions jama karne ki mahaarat bhi chahiye, is liye common denominator wala qadam dhyan se dekhiye.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: Use mathematical induction to prove that \(\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)} = \frac{n}{2n + 1}\), whenever \(n\) is a positive integer.
steps:
Given: \(S(n): \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)} = \frac{n}{2n + 1}\). \(\sum\) (sigma) ka matlab hai "jama karo": \(k = 1\) se \(k = n\) tak har term jama karein:
\[\dfrac{1}{1 \cdot 3} + \dfrac{1}{3 \cdot 5} + \ldots\]
\[+ \dfrac{1}{(2n - 1)(2n + 1)} = \dfrac{n}{2n + 1}\]
To prove: \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye.
Method: induction. Dhyan dein, yahan \(k\) pehle se sum ke andar ginti ke liye istemal ho raha hai, is liye kitab induction step mein \(m\) istemal karti hai.

Step 1: Base case (n = 1)
Sum mein sirf \(k = 1\) wala term hai:
\[\dfrac{1}{1 \cdot 3} = \dfrac{1}{2 \cdot 1 + 1}\]
\[\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Is liye \(S(1)\) sach hai, base case poora.
Kyun: left par \(k = 1\) aur right par \(n = 1\) rakha.

Step 2: Induction hypothesis
Farz karein ke \(n = m\) par \(S(n)\) sach hai:
\[\sum_{k=1}^{m} \dfrac{1}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)} = \dfrac{m}{2m + 1} \quad (A)\]

Step 3: S(m + 1): agla term jama karein
\(k = m + 1\) wala term \(\frac{1}{(2m + 1)(2m + 3)}\) hai. (A) ki madad se:
\[\sum_{k=1}^{m+1} \dfrac{1}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{m}{2m + 1} + \dfrac{1}{(2m + 1)(2m + 3)}\]
Kyun: \(m + 1\) tak ka sum \(= m\) tak ka sum + ek aur term. Agla term nikaalne ke liye \(k = m + 1\) rakhein: \(2(m + 1) - 1 = 2m + 1\) aur \(2(m + 1) + 1 = 2m + 3\).

Step 4: Fractions jama karein
\[= \dfrac{m(2m + 3) + 1}{(2m + 1)(2m + 3)}\]
\[= \dfrac{2m^{2} + 3m + 1}{(2m + 1)(2m + 3)}\]
\[= \dfrac{(m + 1)(2m + 1)}{(2m + 1)(2m + 3)}\]
Kyun: common denominator \((2m + 1)(2m + 3)\) hai, is liye pehle fraction ko \((2m + 3)\) se upar neeche zarb kiya. Phir \(2m^{2} + 3m + 1 = 2m^{2} + 2m + m + 1 = (m + 1)(2m + 1)\), aur \((2m + 1)\) upar neeche cancel ho gaya.

Step 5: n/(2n + 1) wali shakal, n = m + 1 ke saath
\[= \dfrac{m + 1}{2m + 3} = \dfrac{m + 1}{2m + 2 + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{m + 1}{2(m + 1) + 1} \quad (B)\]
Yani jab \(S(m)\) sach ho to \(S(m + 1)\) bhi sach hai.
Kyun: \(\frac{n}{2n + 1}\) mein \(n = m + 1\) rakhein to bilkul \(\frac{m + 1}{2(m + 1) + 1}\) aata hai. \(3\) ko \(2 + 1\) likhna isi shakal ko dikhane ke liye tha.

Step 6: Conclusion
Dono sharatein poori hain, is liye mathematical induction ke usool se \(S(n)\) har positive integer \(n\) (\(n \in \mathbb{N}\)) ke liye sach hai.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)} = \frac{n}{2n + 1}\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 6 mein chaar chhoti ghaltiyan hain:
1. "Thus S(0) is true" chhapa hai; sahi "\(S(1)\) is true" hai, kyun ke base case \(n = 1\) hai.
2. \(S(m + 1)\) mein sum ki upper limit \(m - 1\) chhapi hai; sahi \(m + 1\) hai.
3. "\(S(k + 1)\) is true when \(S(k)\) is true" likha hai, jab ke saboot \(m\) mein hai: sahi "\(S(m + 1)\) sach hai jab \(S(m)\) sach ho".
4. Conclusion mein \(n \in W\) likha hai; statement positive integers ke liye hai, is liye \(n \in \mathbb{N}\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
1. Example 5 mein agar \(n = 4\) ho to \(S(4)\) kitna hai, aur kya yeh 9 se divisible hai? (Jawab: \(256 + 24 - 1 = 279 = 9 \times 31\). Haan.)
2. Example 6 ka sum \(n = 3\) tak kya hai? (Jawab: \(\frac{3}{7}\), kyun ke \(\frac{2}{5} + \frac{1}{35} = \frac{15}{35} = \frac{3}{7}\).)
3. Kya \(n^{2} - n + 41\) wali statement ko induction se saabit kiya ja sakta hai? (Jawab: nahin, kyun ke woh ghalat hai; \(n = 41\) par fail hoti hai. Induction ka step kabhi poora nahin hoga.)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin. Saabit kijiye ke \(2 + 4 + 6 + \ldots + 2n = n(n + 1)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye.
Base case (\(n = 1\)): left side 2, right side \(1(1 + 1) = 2\). Sach.
Hypothesis: farz karein \(2 + 4 + \ldots + 2k = k(k + 1)\). (A)
Manzil: \(2 + 4 + \ldots + 2k + 2(k + 1) = (k + 1)(k + 2)\). (B)
Step: (A) ke dono taraf \(2(k + 1)\) jama karein:
\[k(k + 1) + 2(k + 1) = (k + 1)(k + 2)\]
Common factor \((k + 1)\) nikaala aur (B) mil gaya. Conclusion: formula har \(n\) ke liye sach hai.
Dekhiye, yeh bilkul Example 1 ka hi dhaancha hai; sirf terms badle hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh bhi hamari practice hai. Saabit kijiye ke \(3^{n} - 1\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye 2 se divisible (yani even) hai.
Base case (\(n = 1\)): \(3^{1} - 1 = 2\), jo 2 se divisible hai.
Hypothesis: farz karein \(3^{k} - 1 = 2q\) kisi integer \(q\) ke liye, yani \(3^{k} = 2q + 1\).
Step: \(3^{k + 1} - 1 = 3 \cdot 3^{k} - 1 = 3(2q + 1) - 1 = 6q + 2 = 2(3q + 1)\), jo 2 se divisible hai.
Conclusion: induction se \(3^{n} - 1\) har \(n\) ke liye even hai.
Kyun yeh misaal: yeh bilkul Example 5 wali chaal hai, sirf chhote numbers ke saath, taa ke aap tareeqa pehchan lein: farz ko equation banao, \(3^{k + 1} = 3 \cdot 3^{k}\) likho, substitute karo, aur 2 bahar nikaalo.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Chand sahi misaalein kisi baat ko har \(n\) ke liye saabit nahin kartein (\(n^{2} - n + 41\) \(n = 1\) se 40 tak prime hai, 41 par nahin). Ghalat saabit karne ke liye ek counter example kaafi hai.
2. Mathematical induction ke teen hisse: Base Case (\(S(1)\) sach), Induction of Hypothesis (\(S(k)\) sach \(\Rightarrow\) \(S(k + 1)\) sach) aur Conclusion.
3. Base case wahan se shuru karein jahan se statement shuru ho: aam taur par \(n = 1\), non-negative integers ke liye \(n = 0\) (Example 4).
4. Sum wale saboot mein: \(S(k)\) ko (A), \(S(k + 1)\) ko (B) likhein, (A) ke dono taraf \((k + 1)\)th term jama karein, aur (B) ki right side tak simplify karein. Pehle common factor nikaalna mehnat bachata hai.
5. Divisibility mein: farz ko equation banaein (\(= 9k_{1}\)), \(S(k + 1)\) ko \(4^{k}\) ke zariye likh kar substitute karein (Example 5); ya \(S(k + 1)\) ko \(S(k)\) + koi saaf integer mein todein (Example 3).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Base case chhor dena, ya sirf "\(n = 1\) par true hai" likh dena. Bachne ka tareeqa: dono sides alag alag hisaab kar ke likhiye.
2. \(S(k)\) ko saabit karne baith jana. \(S(k)\) farz hai; saabit \(S(k + 1)\) karna hai.
3. Agla term ghalat likhna. \((k + 1)\)th term general term mein \(n = k + 1\) rakhne se aata hai: Example 1 mein \(3(k + 1)\), Example 2 mein \((k + 1)^{2}\); \(3k + 1\) ya \(k^{2} + 1\) nahin.
4. Naya term (A) ki sirf ek taraf jama karna. Jo left par jama ho, wahi right par bhi jama hona chahiye.
5. Sab kuch khol kar bara polynomial bana lena. Pehle \((k + 1)\) jaisa common factor nikaaliye; hisaab chhota aur saaf rahega.
